source_en: Home after a twelve-hour driving shift.
Home to the western block. Family's waiting.
Dropping the cab at the fleet garage.
Cab won't start. Walking home west.
Checking my building's security.
Hunting a Volga part. Engine's dead again.
Cab's dead in the depot. Going home.
Home to my wife and kids.
Mandatory residency check-in.
First day driving a taxi. Still learning streets.
Walking. Never learned to drive, hate cars.
Pension. Retired from driving last year.
Driving my new car. Purrs like a kitten.
Home alone. Never married, never wanted kids.
Back from my Writers' Union desk.
Driving fares all night. Business is booming.
Home to the eastern district, as always.
Going to my mother's. My only family.
Move it along, officer. I've got a fare and time is money.
What, you need to see my teeth too? Check the damn paper.
My car won't start and the streets are full of junk. Happy now?
We're all breathing the same poison. The booth doesn't make you special.
Go ahead, keep me here. There's nowhere left to drive anyway.
You're a bouncer for a club that's burning down.
Finally. Work a bit faster next time, yeah?
Yeah, yeah. Watch your back. It's getting ugly.
Whatever. Enjoy your little cage while it lasts.
You have GOT to be out of your mind, I swear!
FINE! But on the record, this is completely WRONG!
Of all the small-minded, cowardly…!
You better hope… I don't come back… as a ghost… pal…
Where are you coming from?
Fleet garage. Twelve hours, and the Volga's clutch is shot again. Can I go?
My building, western block. Checked the locks. Cab's dead, so I walked.
Nowhere. Cab's dead in the depot yard. I walked the ash like everybody.
My place on the east side. I could drive that route blind.
A fare out to Varka and back. Car ran like a dream.
My brother's flat. Wife left, no kids, nothing to go home to.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Runny nose. Twelve hours of exhaust does that. Next question.
Dizzy when I stand too fast. It passes. Don't write that down.
My ears ring all day and night. Sirens or me. Who cares?
Healthy as a horse. Haven't driven in months, no fumes.
Two weeks in bed with a fever. Haven't left the flat once.
Clean lungs. Gave up the cab years ago. I push papers now.
Move it along, would you? Twelve minutes I've been standing here.
Someone should sort out the roads in this district. Absolute mess.
My cab doesn't start anymore. Three years I kept that engine running.
Half the streets are blocked now. Your people closed them.
Take your time. Not like the world's ending or anything.
Still stamping papers? Fine. Stamp the paper. I'll wait.
